introduction:
House and Land Documents typically refer to Property Registration, which is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. Registering your property ensures legal ownership and protects against disputes in Madhya Pradesh.

The registration process involves paying stamp duty and registration fees, and must be completed at the local Sub-Registrar's Office within 4 months of the execution of the sale deed. It serves as an undeniable record of title and rights over the property.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts
  • Service: Application for Property Registration online in Madhya Pradesh (2026 process).
  • Cost: 7.5% Stamp Duty + 3% Registration Fee (Total 10.5% of the property guideline or market value, whichever is higher). Search/Processing fees may apply.
  • Portal Used: SAMPADA 2.0 (MPIGR)
  • Authentication Method: Aadhaar OTP-based login, biometric verification, and Video KYC.
  • Important Requirement: The applicant's Aadhaar card must be linked to an active mobile number to receive OTPs for e-Signatures.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Note: All documents must be uploaded digitally in clear formats (PDF, JPG). Ensure you have originals ready for final verification.
For Buyer, Seller, & Witnesses
  • Identity Proof: Aadhaar Card (Highly recommended for e-KYC), PAN Card (Mandatory if the transaction is over ₹50 Lakh), Voter ID, or Passport.
  • Address Proof: Aadhaar Card, Passport, or Bank Passbook.
Property & Additional Proofs
  • Primary Instrument: Original Sale Deed or drafted property agreement.
  • Previous Title Documents: Chain of ownership for resale properties.
  • Encumbrance Certificate: To confirm the property has no prior legal liabilities.
  • Property Tax Receipts: Proof of current tax payment status.
  • Property Photographs: Front, left, and right views (SAMPADA 2.0 uses GIS to match geo-coordinates).
  • Property Map/Approved Layout: For plot or building identification.
  • Diversion Certificate: If converting agricultural land for residential use.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Registration via SAMPADA 2.0

Step 1: Portal Login
  1. Visit the official SAMPADA 2.0 portal (sampada.mpigr.gov.in).
  2. Click on "Login" at the top right and select "Public Users".
  3. Register as a 'New User' or 'Civil Registration' using your Aadhaar details, mobile number, and email.
  4. Verify via the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number to log into your dashboard.
Step 2: Property Valuation
  1. Navigate to "Property Valuation" on your dashboard.
  2. Enter the district, tehsil, ward/colony details, and select the property type (Plot, Building, or Agricultural).
  3. The system will use GIS to fetch the area's government guideline rate and generate a Valuation ID.
Step 3: Initiating Registration Steps
  1. Registration Initiation: Select the type of deed (e.g., Sale Deed, Gift Deed) and enter the Valuation ID.
  2. Party Details: Fill in the personal details, Aadhaar numbers, and contact info for the buyer, seller, and two witnesses.
  3. Upload Documents: Upload the mandatory ID proofs, property photographs, maps, and the drafted sale deed.
  4. Calculate & Pay: The system will calculate the Stamp Duty (7.5%) and Registration Fee (3%). Pay this amount online via the integrated Cyber Treasury (NetBanking, Card, or SAMPADA Wallet) to generate an E-Stamp.
Step 4: Final Submission and Slot Booking
  1. Once the payment is confirmed, submit the application.
  2. Proceed to book a time slot for final verification. You can opt for a physical visit to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) or choose the new "Video KYC" (Faceless Registration) option.
Step 5: Offline Visit Required (or Video KYC)
  1. If a physical visit is booked, the buyer, seller, and witnesses must visit the SRO with all original documents at the scheduled time.
  2. All parties will undergo biometric authentication (fingerprints and photos) at the office.
  3. If Video KYC is selected, parties must verify their identities live via camera on the portal instead of visiting the office.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Traditional Offline Registration

Note: While SAMPADA 2.0 makes the process primarily digital, here is the traditional procedure if dealing directly through the office.
  1. Visit your jurisdictional Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) in Madhya Pradesh.
  2. Hire a certified deed writer or legal advocate to draft the Sale Deed on standard stamp paper or E-stamp.
  3. Calculate the required Stamp Duty and Registration charges manually based on the Collector's Guideline Value.
  4. Purchase the required E-Stamps from an authorized vendor or bank.
  5. Present the drafted deed, attached with all ID proofs, property maps, and tax receipts, to the Sub-Registrar.
  6. The buyer, seller, and two witnesses must sign the document in front of the Sub-Registrar and provide biometric thumb impressions.
  7. Collect the registration receipt. The original registered deed will be handed over or mailed after processing.
afterApplying:
After Registering & Next Steps

  • You can track the status of your registry through your SAMPADA 2.0 dashboard.
  • Once approved, a soft copy of the registered deed (PDF) is sent directly to your email and WhatsApp.
  • You can also navigate to "Document Search/Certified Copy" on the portal to download a certified digital copy anytime.
  • After receiving the registry, apply for "Mutation" (Namantaran) through the MP Bhulekh portal or local municipal office to update your name in the government land records.
